subject: Post-demo: deployment bakeoff & GPU sprint plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vectorlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo: deployment bakeoff & GPU sprint plan

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the hosted vs dedicated vs private options and nail the GPU sizing:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary need: low-latency inference for user-facing chat with occasional long-document ops (search/summarize).
- Current traffic expectation: steady-state ~80 req/s with spiky bursts up to ~350 req/s for 1–3 minute windows.
- Average token mix: ~120 tokens per request; ~10% of calls touch long context (~2k tokens).
- Compliance: SOC2 + internal VPC requirement for production.

Open questions we need from you (so our sizing workshop is productive)
1) Confirm 95th-pct latency SLO target (we heard ~150ms p95 — confirm?).
2) Provide a short sample prompt set or anonymized logs (3–5 minutes of representative requests) — we included token_profile.csv as a template.
3) Clarify procurement timing and any vendor constraints for on-prem hosting.

Redwood recommendation (initial, pre-bakeoff):
- Best fit likely Dedicated capacity with Private VPC for compliance and predictable throughput.
- GPU strategy: mixed pool with H100s for throughput-critical routes and A100s for cost-sensitive low-concurrency routes. We will validate in the workshop.

Proposed next steps
- Sizing workshop (90 min): deep-dive on token mix, concurrency, and model variants; we can run a short synthetic load test during the session. Proposed slots: Thu Oct 29 or Mon Nov 2 — which works for your infra + security folks?
- Deliverable: a short bakeoff plan + cost/latency trade-off matrix and a 2-week canary plan for Dedicated + VPC. Attachment: deployment_bakeoff_table.xlsx; token_profile.csv (template)

If you can confirm the three asks above and pick a slot, we’ll lock the workshop and loop in our infra engineering (Ben/Karthik) and solutions lead (Aditya).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

--

Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 16:34:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment bakeoff & GPU sprint plan

Hannah, thanks — great recap. Answers inline below: 

- Latency SLO: yes, target p95 <= 150ms for short-chat turn (100–200 tokens). For long-context jobs (>=1500 tokens) we are OK with p95 <= 800ms.
- Traffic: confirmed steady ~80 rps, typical peak ~320–380 rps for 1–3 minutes tied to product launches. Bursts are highly spiky but infrequent (2–3x per week).
- Token mix: your template works — we attached a sanitized sample (see security_faq.pdf for note on what we redacted). Avg tokens ~120; 10–12% long-context as you noted.
- Compliance & procurement: We need Private VPC (must terminate inside our cloud account) and SOC2 evidence; procurement timetable is ~6–8 weeks after SOW. On-prem is not realistic for now, but Dedicated w/ customer VPC (or Redwood-hosted but inside our VPC via private peering) is acceptable.

We’re good to run the workshop. Thu Oct 29 at 16:00 PT works for our team (I’ll invite infra/security).

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of ML Platforms
Vectorlytics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 17:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment bakeoff & GPU sprint plan

Hannah —

Thanks for the note and Sam for the quick answers. My high-level take after reading the sample profile:

1) Deployment mode: Dedicated + Private VPC is the right starting point given SOC2 + VPC requirement and bursty peaks. Hosted-only would struggle to guarantee the isolation/procurement timelines they need.

2) GPU mix recommendation (initial hypothesis):
   - H100s (sparse/matrix-optimized variants) for the high-throughput chat route to hit 150ms p95 at scale for short-context calls. H100 gives better perf at high concurrency and for long prompt encode/decode.
   - A100 80GB (quantized) nodes for lower-cost asynchronous long-context jobs and background tasks that tolerate slightly higher latency.
   - We should consider a small pool of lower-cost LLM accelerators (L40ish or older A100-like instances) for batch inference / offline rerank to save cost.

3) Concurrency/throughput plan:
   - Steady 80 rps baseline — map to single-digit number of H100 instances depending on model size and batch behavior.
   - Plan for burst capacity: autoscaling policy + a small buffer of reserved burst GPUs (to cover 2–3 minute spikes). We can quantify exact instance counts in the workshop when we run the synthetic baseline.

4) Action items for workshop (Karthik / Aditya):
   - Karthik: prepare model-level perf estimates for H100 vs A100 for the family of models they mentioned (include expected tokens/sec and memory/KV cache implications).
   - Aditya: draft the 2-week canary runbook (metrics, rollback criteria, data flows for VPC peering).

I’ll bring an initial cost/latency matrix to the workshop (H100 vs A100 vs hybrid). If we want aggressive cost control, we can recommend quantized variants and caching; Karthik will outline quantization impact.

Ben
Director, Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference
